The folder name '同PT5生物相容性报告' (same as PT5 biocompatibility report) suggests an intent to reuse PT5 data, but no formal equivalence or bridging record is present in the supplied evidence.
challenge_questions: Is there a formal biocompatibility bridging justification document that establishes material equivalence between PT5 and PT9L contact components, and if so, what is its document number and approval status?
Are the ABS, TPU, PMMA, and PC materials used in PT9L sourced from the same suppliers and to the same specifications as those tested for PT5?
Has a ISO 10993-1:2018 biological evaluation plan been completed for PT9L that explicitly references the PT5 test data as supporting evidence?
Does the 510(k) submission for PT9L include a biocompatibility section, and if so, which test reports are cited — PT5 reports or PT9L-specific reports?

findings.claim: The PT9L operation guide (F0083) references the Medical Device Directive (MDD) for biocompatibility compliance rather than the Medical Device Regulation (MDR 2017/745), which has been the applicable EU framework since May 2021; this is inconsistent with the current regulatory environment even though the design input marks EU/MDR as not applicable for the current market scope.
findings.rationale: REG-074 (F0083 line 162) states contact materials 'are in compliance with the Medical Device Directive (MDD) requirements.' MDD was repealed and replaced by MDR 2017/745 effective May 26, 2021. REG-064 (F0031) and REG-130 (F0121) both mark MDR 2017/745 as not applicable (□是 ■否) for the current design scope, and REG-059 and REG-117 confirm the intended market is FDA/US only. However, the operation guide is a customer-facing document that may be distributed globally, and citing a repealed directive creates a regulatory accuracy issue regardless of current market scope. REG-076 (F0083 line 466) also references the 2012/19/EU WEEE Directive for EU battery disposal, indicating the guide is intended for EU distribution contexts.
challenge_questions: Is the PT9L operation guide (F0083) intended for distribution in EU markets, and if so, has a CE marking or MDR conformity assessment been initiated?
Has the MDD reference in the operation guide been identified as a labeling nonconformity in any design review or label review record?
The label review document (F0082) references IEC 60601-1-11 and ISO 80601-2-56 compliance — does this label review also cover the operation guide text, and was the MDD reference reviewed?
If EU distribution is planned in the future, what is the change control process for updating the operation guide to reference MDR 2017/745?

findings.claim: Both ASTM E1965-98:2016 and ASTM E1965-98:2023 are listed as applicable standards in the design input (F0031), design verification plan (F0121), and design verification report (F0114), and both are marked as passing in the label review (F0082), but no transition rationale, gap analysis, or documented justification for maintaining dual-version compliance is present in the supplied evidence.
findings.rationale: REG-062 and REG-063 (F0031) list both ASTM E1965-98:2016 and ASTM E1965-98:2023 as applicable US standards. REG-128 and REG-129 (F0121) and REG-121 and REG-122 (F0114) repeat this dual citation with both marked as applicable and passing. REG-071 (F0082) shows ASTM E1965-98:2023 as passing in the label review. REG-073 (F0083) cites 'ISO 80601-2-56:2017+A1:2018 and ASTM Standard(E1965-98)' without specifying which year edition. No gap analysis, transition plan, or justification document explaining why both editions are simultaneously applicable is present in the supplied evidence catalog.
challenge_questions: What are the substantive differences between ASTM E1965-98:2016 and ASTM E1965-98:2023, and has a gap analysis been performed to confirm PT9L meets both editions?
The external test reports cited in the design verification report (ETX202303-07-078-03/04) — do they test against ASTM E1965-98:2016, ASTM E1965-98:2023, or both?
Is the dual-version citation a transitional measure pending a single-version determination, and if so, what is the target date for resolution?
Does the 510(k) submission cite both ASTM editions, and has FDA provided any guidance on which edition is currently recognized?

findings.claim: The project profile states that 510(k) registration responsibility lies with 'andon' as the responsible and paying party, but no 510(k) submission agreement, regulatory responsibility assignment, or formal record of this arrangement is present in the supplied evidence catalog.
findings.rationale: The project profile regulatory baseline entry states '510(k) registration: andon responsible and paying.' REG-059 and REG-117 confirm the intended market is FDA/US only (■ FDA 对应地区：美国). No document in the evidence catalog — including the design input (F0031), design verification plan (F0121), or any risk management document — contains a reference to a 510(k) submission agreement, regulatory agency agreement, or formal record identifying 'andon' as the 510(k) holder. The absence of this record means the regulatory responsibility chain for the primary target market cannot be verified from the DHF.
challenge_questions: Is there a written agreement between the manufacturer and 'andon' (iHealth/Jiuan Medical) that assigns 510(k) submission responsibility, and if so, what is its document number and where is it filed in the DHF?
Who will be listed as the 510(k) submitter and device owner in the FDA submission — the manufacturer or andon?
Has the 510(k) submission been filed, and if so, what is the submission number (K-number)?
Does the quality management system require a regulatory responsibility agreement to be included in the DHF for FDA-targeted products?
